_comment: Ground-truth labels for the benchmark corpus.
The detector sees only corpus.json. These attributes — what input a method
needs, what a dataset provides, and which body region each concerns — are
held out. A transfer gap is genuine only if the untried pairing is actually
runnable; the detector has no way to know that, so the gap between its
output and this file is exactly what the eval measures.

limitation_gaps._comment: Hand-labelled. True when the limitation is pervasive across the methods tried on that problem, i.e. no existing approach escapes it.

true.why: All seven papers report it, across four distinct method families.
All five papers report it; inherent to monocular hand capture.
Reported by five of six papers, including every SMPL-based one.

false.why: Confined to the diffusion papers; hourglass and GNN methods are fast, so it is a property of one method family rather than an open problem.
Only the temporal variant reports it. Single-frame methods are unaffected.
Only arises on two-hand datasets; single-hand work does not face it.

future_work_gaps._comment: Hand-labelled. True when the corpus repeatedly asks for a direction that nothing in the corpus delivers.

true.why: Requested by six papers spanning all three problems, and no corpus method covers hands and body jointly.
Requested by five papers; no method in the corpus imposes physical plausibility.

false.why: Requested twice, but temporal_smoothing already delivers it in three papers. The detector matches labels to method names literally, so it cannot see that this is already realised under a different name.
Requested four times, but is an efficiency ask against known methods rather than an unexplored direction.
